title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten Lawrence spaces with documented uses for studying, making, viewing, meeting, reflecting, and displaying student work.

cards.title: Spread Out Between the Science Buildings
cards.subtitle: First-floor link between Youngchild and Steitz halls
cards.notes: Bring group work that benefits from a table and daylight; the atrium linking the science buildings has both, according to Lawrence.
cards.short_summary: A bright, table-equipped study area joining Lawrence’s two science buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: Lawrence identifies the Science Atrium as the first-floor connection between Youngchild and Steitz halls and says it has tables, chairs, and natural light for studying.
cards.source_title: Our favorite study spots on campus
cards.access_notes: The university describes student access; consult current building access information before visiting outside normal academic activity.

cards.title: Pair Lounge Seating With Meeting Space
cards.subtitle: Student-organization level of Warch Campus Center
cards.notes: Use the tables or couches for everyday work, and check the campus reservation system before counting on either meeting room.
cards.short_summary: A flexible student floor combining casual seating, meeting rooms, and computer access.
cards.evidence_claim: Lawrence says Warch’s fourth floor contains tables, chairs, couches, two student-available meeting rooms, a computer, and a printer.
cards.source_title: Our favorite study spots on campus
cards.access_notes: Meeting-room availability may depend on reservations; follow current Warch access and scheduling rules.

cards.title: Choose a Quieter Place to Reflect or Read
cards.subtitle: Campus house supporting religious and spiritual life
cards.notes: Settle into the seating for quiet reading or reflection, while respecting programs and the house’s primary spiritual-life purpose.
cards.short_summary: A meditative campus house that Lawrence also documents as a quiet study setting.
cards.evidence_claim: Lawrence describes Sabin House as a place for students to explore religious identity and as a quiet study space furnished with couches, rolling chairs, and a kitchen.
cards.source_title: Our favorite study spots on campus
cards.access_notes: Use is for students and should accommodate scheduled spiritual-life activities; verify current access before arrival.

cards.title: Watch for Free Campus Screenings
cards.subtitle: Second level of Warch Campus Center
cards.notes: Check the university event listing for the next screening or large program; the cinema sits on Warch’s second level.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated campus cinema used for complimentary screenings and other large events.
cards.evidence_claim: The current Warch Campus Center page states that the second-level Warch Cinema hosts free film screenings and other large events.
cards.access_notes: Entry depends on the scheduled event and its stated audience; consult the current Lawrence events listing.

cards.title: Edit Audio or Work Through a Score
cards.subtitle: Room 116 on the Mudd Library first floor
cards.notes: Bring a score or audio project and use the piano, MIDI workstations, scanners, or listening equipment suited to the task.
cards.short_summary: A community-accessible music workspace with production, scanning, and playback tools.
cards.evidence_claim: Lawrence says Room 116 is available to all members of its community and provides a digital piano, MIDI workstations, composition software, scanners, and listening equipment.
cards.access_notes: Available to Lawrence community members during library access; individual equipment may already be in use.

cards.title: Move Up to a Silent Room
cards.subtitle: Fourth floor of Seeley G. Mudd Library
cards.notes: Choose this room when conversation would be distracting; Lawrence specifically designates it for silent study or reflection.
cards.short_summary: A named fourth-floor room reserved in practice for silence and reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: The library’s current spaces page identifies the fourth floor as silent study and specifically designates the Kruse Room for silent study or reflection.
cards.access_notes: Observe the silent-study designation and current Mudd Library entry requirements and building hours.

cards.title: Reserve the Right Setup for Media Work
cards.subtitle: Four first-floor rooms in Seeley G. Mudd Library
cards.notes: Sign up at the room door for a viewing or presentation session, remembering that academic media use receives priority.
cards.short_summary: Reservable rooms equipped for disc, tape, laptop, and presentation playback.
cards.evidence_claim: Lawrence documents four first-floor viewing rooms with Blu-ray/DVD players, VCRs, monitors, and laptop connections, reservable in 2.5-hour sessions by students with ID access.
cards.access_notes: Lawrence ID access is required. Reserve in person on the posted schedule; academic viewing and listening take priority.

cards.title: Look for an Unscheduled Historic Room
cards.subtitle: Special-collections room in Seeley G. Mudd Library
cards.notes: Check whether the room is between scheduled functions, then use it for individual or group study on a first-come basis.
cards.short_summary: A named special-collections room that doubles as study space when unbooked.
cards.evidence_claim: Lawrence says the Milwaukee-Downer Room is available for individual or group study on a first-come, first-served basis when it is not otherwise in use.
cards.access_notes: Academic or administrative functions take precedence; confirm the room is unoccupied before settling in.

cards.title: Prototype Instead of Just Taking Notes
cards.subtitle: First floor of Seeley G. Mudd Library
cards.notes: Bring a making project to the library’s first floor and review current equipment guidance before beginning hands-on work.
cards.short_summary: Lawrence’s library-based workspace for engaged, hands-on learning.
cards.evidence_claim: The current library spaces page identifies the first-floor Makerspace as Lawrence’s campus makerspace for engaged learning.
cards.access_notes: Access and equipment use are governed by current library and makerspace instructions; training may apply to particular tools.

cards.title: See Where Students Learn to Mount Exhibitions
cards.subtitle: Third floor of Seeley G. Mudd Library
cards.notes: Visit the third floor to see the current installation, or contact the university if you want to propose displaying student work.
cards.short_summary: A library gallery where student exhibitions become practical curatorial experience.
cards.evidence_claim: Lawrence identifies Mudd Gallery as a third-floor space where students display work and gain experience installing exhibitions, including solo and course shows.
cards.source_title: Mudd Gallery, Art & Artifacts in the Library
cards.access_notes: View during current library access hours; exhibition proposals and installations require coordination with university staff.
